speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These professionals play a key role in the development of special needs children, and we support them in several ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Professionals working in the special needs sector must hold the relevant degrees or diplomas in their fields of practice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These range from broad-based courses to targeted ones focusing on the skills and knowledge required to work with special needs clients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, teachers working with children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) can take up targeted courses that build specialised knowledge in autism.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To further upgrade themselves, in-service professionals can also apply for professional development sponsorships, such as the Ministry of Education (MOE) Scholarship for SPED teachers and SkillsFuture Study Awards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Promising social workers and Early Intervention (EI) teachers taking up managerial and leadership positions can also apply for the Professional Development and Management Programme and the Leadership Development Programme which fund leadership, management and other skills-based training.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Second, we also help professionals learn from one another’s experiences and expertise through practice networks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The National Council of Social Service (NCSS) organises annual sessions for social workers and psychologists in SPED schools to share resources and best practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: SPED schools have also put in place Professional Learning Teams (PLTs) where teachers and other professionals can discuss how to improve teaching practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Third, we have put in place measures to help social service professionals cope with the challenges of their jobs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mentoring and on-the-job coaching by senior practitioners also help to alleviate burnout by equipping younger teachers and social workers with skills and strategies to build up their confidence and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, SPED schools have mentoring and coaching programmes for teachers and ensure that teachers have access to counselling services and enjoy protected time during school holidays.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To complement these targeted efforts, NCSS has also been working with VWOs to improve their human resource management capabilities to ensure that all our professionals are well-deployed and cared for, as they give their best to help those in need.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does the Government envisage that there is a need to increase the number of professionals working in the special needs sector and, if so, what are the plans in the next five years?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, it is not only now that we realise that there has been an increase.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, a few years ago, we had anticipated this and the number of professionals in the social service sector has increased significantly for some, depending on the sub-sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And we are mindful that the numbers or the needs require this increase.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, we recognise this and we have been doing that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I assure Members that we are keeping a close watch on how we can, one, care for people; and two, make sure that we provide the necessary framework, infrastructure as well as manpower to ensure that their needs are met sufficiently.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a desirable student-to-teacher ratio that the Ministry is trying to achieve?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a maximum number of hours a teacher can teach within a day, so that they can have a reprieve and have breaks in between?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The unique state of affairs of the disability sector is that the nature of work is complex and it varies from student to student.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, we are very mindful of the needs of the students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For some who have high care needs, we will put more staff to be involved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are also mindful that staff also need reprieve.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, depending on the setting, NCSS and the Ministry of Social and Family Development work closely with the VWOs to see how we can provide the support, not only to the kids but also to the teachers.
